versionStatus: Unreleased development source; not a published-package measurement
scope: 122 selected cells: 83 in the 14-row README table and 39 supplementary; Immediate notification unsupported

conditions.statistic: BDN overhead-adjusted arithmetic mean and managed allocated bytes per operation; not independent-run medians
conditions.confidenceLevel: The retained BDN Level value 12 is an enum, not 12 percent.

provenance.note: Product identities are from the measured children, not the preliminary workspace builds. Original raw reports and saved consumer bundles are retained separately; this file publishes numerical observations and hash bindings, not those binaries or bundles.

validation.scope: Saved-consumer and semantic evidence belongs to the measured source. It is not a new documentation-head CI, full unit-suite, Native AOT performance or released-package validation.

limitations: One machine and one launch per case; no universal ranking or controlled release-to-release improvement. Source, SDK, peers and harness differ from older comparisons.
Time and allocation are separate metrics; all selected unfavorable and supplementary results are retained.
API and DI registration shapes differ. Foundatio uses its intercepted path.
Zendiator Stream and Relay use the named WorkStreamCursor; peers use the shared compiler iterator Work.Stream. These are whole product paths, not an isolated dispatcher or same-producer comparison.
At Stream depth 5 Zendiator forwards its upstream cursor while peers enumerate/yield per stage. Relay matches preprocessing-only stage work but still differs in input representation.
New-scope cases include scope creation, first resolution, send and disposal. FirstSend uses pre-created scopes and excludes scope creation/disposal.
Stream values include complete consumption/disposal; EarlyBreak consumes one item from a 16-item input. Hook first/warm/outer-failure cases have separate boundaries.
The original strict performance/non-regression goals and accepted adoption tradeoffs remain separate; this single-revision run does not overturn them.
